title: Farouk El-Baz, 'the king' of Apollo site selection

tellings.quote: Farouk El-Baz, who oversaw lunar science planning and helped select Apollo landing sites, was nicknamed the king by the astronauts. His father was a scholar of Egyptian religion.

plain: Farouk El-Baz, a scientist who oversaw moon science planning for NASA in the 1960s and helped choose where the Apollo missions to the moon would land, was nicknamed "the king" by the astronauts. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, and adds that El-Baz's father was a scholar of Egyptian religion. He raises it in an episode about pagan ritual and secret science at NASA, as a hint of ancient religion near the heart of the moon programme.
